creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Claude Code 2.1.299 draws each finished Bash call as one row, `· $ <command>…`, cut off with an ellipsis at the pane's width. The second pattern in claude.toml's `live_turn_working` matches any line that starts with a spinner glyph (`·` is one) and ends in `…`, so it reads that row as the spinner. A turn whose last 12 non-empty lines include such a row stays `working` after it ends: the Stop hook's idle report is never confirmed by the rules and expires, and the rules then hold `working` indefinitely.

The doorbell defers messages while a pane is working, so nothing rings that agent until something else redraws its screen. On 2026-10-13 tai-integrator sat at `working` from 22:24 to 23:03 and muster-integrator from 22:21, with every post from their slots and from PARKAN held (`msg.posted` with `deferred` set, no `turn_ended`). Integrators hit this most because they end turns on long `muster pane send` and `git` commands.

Hotfix in place on the owner's laptop: `~/.muster/agent-detection/claude.toml`, the built-in manifest at version 2026.10.13.1 with the timerless branch narrowed to spinner text that is plain words:

    (?:\S.*…\s+\(\d+[smh](?:\s|·)|\p{L}[\w ,’-]*…\s*$)

The daemon loaded it, both integrators' turns ended within a second, and every held message rang. A built-in manifest with a newer version supersedes the override, but delete the file once the fix ships.

To do: take the same change into the built-in manifest, and record a 2.1.299 screen with a turn ending on a truncated Bash row into the detection corpus (`tools/detection-capture.py`), since the corpus has no 2.1.299 capture and no timerless spinner line, so nothing tests either branch today.
title: 🐛 A finished Claude Code turn reads as working when its last lines are long Bash calls, and messages for it are held
